commits.message:
A template's hold reaches the frame only through what it draws or decides (rich-animation-27tq.0gd) (#521)

* A template's hold reaches the frame only through what it draws or decides (rich-animation-27tq.0gd)

`tween`, `loop`, `stepped`, `frames` and `glyphs` no longer stamp cells or
tell the frame themselves. Each marks its return with the hold it is in
(`marked`, go-template-js 0.11.0's evaluation provenance), and
`animationFuncs` returns, beside its functions, the two engine hooks the
engine reports the marks through: `emitted` stamps every emitted fragment
with the holds of the animated values its action read; `decided` tells
`TemplateFrame.onHold` of a mark an if/with/range consumed, whichever arm it
took. A value a template computes and never draws or decides on reports
nothing, so a still bar never claims to move, and a hold is carried through
every variable, printf, comparison, sprig call and template invocation the
value passes, where a stamp on the fragment was lost.

`textFrameAt` is removed: its only callers were the two template functions.
`AnimationFuncs` is the engine's own `EngineConfig` fields, so a hook's
signature is written once.

The peer range stays at ^0.10.0 in this commit: 0.11.0 is tagged and merged
upstream but its npm publish failed for want of a Trusted Publisher, so the
lockfile cannot follow yet. The bump and the lockfile land together once the
registry has it; until then the branch is built against a tarball packed from
the v0.11.0 tag.

* withAnimation installs the functions and their hooks in one call (rich-animation-27tq.0gd)

The high review of PR #521 found that animationFuncs returned the five
functions and the two engine hooks as three config fields a consumer wires
by hand, and that wiring only `funcs` compiles, draws and never says it
moves: every hold vanishes with nothing to say so. The binding is now
`withAnimation(config, frame, options)`, the consumer's engine config with
the functions merged into its `funcs` and `emitted`/`decided` chained over
any the config already carries, so the functions and the hooks that report
for them cannot be wired apart, and a consumer's own hooks still hear
everything they did.

Also from that review: `emitted` hands back a fragment no hold reaches
instead of copying on every emission; `drawn` returns the marked value, so
the five functions no longer each unpack and re-mark it, and `stepped` maps
the beat to its hex inside the animation; the docs and `TemplateFrame` say
what `onHold` hears by the engine's rule — a decision, a writing function,
a throwing action — rather than decisions alone. The gate the review asked
for, that `src/` compiles against the lowest peer the range admits, is
filed as rich-unfiled-791c.25dh.

* withAnimation refuses a config that already has one of its names (rich-animation-27tq.0gd)

* Engine configs for RichText pass isT, the predicate go-template-js 0.12.0 requires (rich-animation-27tq.0gd)

go-template-js 0.12.0 requires isT on any EngineConfig whose T is not a string, so the devDependency and peer floor move to 0.12.0. The engine now prints a plain object as Go prints it, so the smoke test asserts that instead of the old [error] line.

* A throwing decided hook still tells the frame its holds, and isT sits on its own line (rich-animation-27tq.0gd)

Review of 33f4241f3 found the frame was not told when a consumer's decided hook threw. The told call now runs in finally. isT moves onto its own line in the multi-line configs, and the smoke test records why a plain object prints instead of erroring.
